subject: traits convenience struct for propto calcs with examples

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: traits convenience struct for propto calcs with examples
parts:
I just added a file:

src/stan/prob/traits.hpp

It contains a single metaprogram to calculate whether or
not to use a summand in a probability calculation.

Given Daniel's factoring of error policy and tests and
our inclusion of propto as a boolean param, we've now reduced
the normal density to a single manageable and comprehensible
function! Here's the code, which includes examples of
the propto metaprogram in use:

template <bool propto = false,
typename T_y, typename T_loc, typename T_scale,
class Policy = policy<> >

inline typename promote_args<T_y,T_loc,T_scale>::type

normal_log(const T_y& y, const T_loc& mu, const T_scale& sigma,
const Policy& = Policy()) {

static const char* function = "stan::prob::normal_log<%1%>(%1%)";

typename promote_args<T_y,T_loc,T_scale>::type lp(0.0);

if (!check_scale(function, sigma, &lp, Policy()))
return lp;

if (!check_location(function, mu, &lp, Policy()))
return lp;

if (!check_x(function, y, &lp, Policy()))
return lp;

if (include_summand<propto,T_y,T_loc,T_scale>::value)
lp -= square(y - mu) / (2.0 * square(sigma));

if (include_summand<propto,T_scale>::value)
lp -= log(sigma);

if (include_summand<propto>::value)
lp += NEG_LOG_SQRT_TWO_PI;

return lp;
}

Metaprogramming's the bomb once you get your head around it.
I also used it to shrink the tests to a manageable size.

And check out Boost's groovy trick on the policy arg. Because
Policy is always a sizeless struct, this basically lets the
compiler ignore all the passing of Policy args and manage everything
statically through the types. (It took Daniel and I a while to
even figure out what this pattern from Boost was doing.)

- Bob
